# Context:
The coordinator of an exhibition will select at least four and at most six rugs from a group of eight rugs made up of two oval wool rugs, three rectangular wool rugs, one oval silk rug, and two rectangular silk rugs according to the following conditions: At least two oval rugs must be selected. The number of wool rugs selected can be neither less than two nor more than three. If the oval silk rug is selected, at least one rectangular silk rug must be selected.

# Question:
If exactly six rugs are selected, they must include

# Options:
A) exactly one of the oval rugs
B) the two oval wool rugs
C) the two rectangular silk rugs
D) exactly three of the rectangular rugs
E) all three rectangular wool rugs

from z3 import *

# Declarations
# The coordinator of an exhibition will select at least four and at most six rugs from a group of eight rugs made up of two oval wool rugs, three rectangular wool rugs, one oval silk rug, and two rectangular silk rugs according to the following conditions
rugs_sort, (oval_wool1, oval_wool2, rectangular_wool1, rectangular_wool2, rectangular_wool3, oval_silk, rectangular_silk1, rectangular_silk2) = EnumSort('rugs', ['oval_wool1', 'oval_wool2', 'rectangular_wool1', 'rectangular_wool2', 'rectangular_wool3', 'oval_silk', 'rectangular_silk1', 'rectangular_silk2'])
rugs = [oval_wool1, oval_wool2, rectangular_wool1, rectangular_wool2, rectangular_wool3, oval_silk, rectangular_silk1, rectangular_silk2]
selected = Function('selected', rugs_sort, BoolSort())

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# At least four rugs must be selected
pre_conditions.append(Sum([selected(r) for r in rugs]) >= 4)
# At most six rugs must be selected
pre_conditions.append(Sum([selected(r) for r in rugs]) <= 6)
# At least two oval rugs must be selected
pre_conditions.append(Sum([And(selected(r), Or(r == oval_wool1, r == oval_wool2, r == oval_silk)) for r in rugs]) >= 2)
# The number of wool rugs selected can be neither less than two nor more than three
pre_conditions.append(Sum([And(selected(r), Or(r == oval_wool1, r == oval_wool2, r == rectangular_wool1, r == rectangular_wool2, r == rectangular_wool3)) for r in rugs]) >= 2)
# The number of wool rugs selected can be neither less than two nor more than three
pre_conditions.append(Sum([And(selected(r), Or(r == oval_wool1, r == oval_wool2, r == rectangular_wool1, r == rectangular_wool2, r == rectangular_wool3)) for r in rugs]) <= 3)
# If the oval silk rug is selected, at least one rectangular silk rug must be selected
r = Const('r', rugs_sort)
pre_conditions.append(Implies(selected(oval_silk), Exists([r], And(r != oval_silk, Or(r == rectangular_silk1, r == rectangular_silk2), selected(r)))))
# Exactly six rugs are selected
pre_conditions.append(Sum([selected(r) for r in rugs]) == 6)

# Question: If exactly six rugs are selected, they must include
def is_valid(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(Not(option_constraints))
    return solver.check() == unsat


# A) exactly one of the oval rugs
if is_valid(Sum([And(selected(r), Or(r == oval_wool1, r == oval_wool2, r == oval_silk)) for r in rugs]) == 1): print('(A)')
# B) the two oval wool rugs
if is_valid(And(selected(oval_wool1), selected(oval_wool2))): print('(B)')
# C) the two rectangular silk rugs
if is_valid(And(selected(rectangular_silk1), selected(rectangular_silk2))): print('(C)')
# D) exactly three of the rectangular rugs
if is_valid(Sum([And(selected(r), Or(r == rectangular_wool1, r == rectangular_wool2, r == rectangular_wool3, r == rectangular_silk1, r == rectangular_silk2)) for r in rugs]) == 3): print('(D)')
# E) all three rectangular wool rugs
if is_valid(And(selected(rectangular_wool1), selected(rectangular_wool2), selected(rectangular_wool3))): print('(E)')

# Declarations
# The seven members of an academic department are each to be assigned a different room as an office. The department members are professors F and G, lecturers Q, R, and S, and instructors V and W. The available rooms are seven consecutive rooms along one side of a straight hallway numbered sequentially 101 through 107.
members_sort, (F, G, Q, R, S, V, W) = EnumSort('members', ['F', 'G', 'Q', 'R', 'S', 'V', 'W'])
rooms_sort = IntSort()
members = [F, G, Q, R, S, V, W]
rooms = [101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107]
assigned = Function('assigned', members_sort, rooms_sort)

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# each member is assigned a different room
m1 = Const('m1', members_sort)
m2 = Const('m2', members_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([m1, m2], Implies(m1 != m2, assigned(m1) != assigned(m2))))
# Neither instructor is assigned a room next to a professor's room
m = Const('m', members_sort)
p = Const('p', members_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([m], Implies(Or(m == V, m == W), ForAll([p], Implies(Or(p == F, p == G), Abs(assigned(m) - assigned(p)) > 1)))))
# Neither professor is assigned room 101 and neither professor is assigned room 107
p = Const('p', members_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([p], Implies(Or(p == F, p == G), And(assigned(p) != 101, assigned(p) != 107))))
# G is not assigned a room next to R's room
m = Const('m', members_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([m], Implies(m == G, Abs(assigned(m) - assigned(R)) > 1)))
# W is not assigned a room next to V's room unless R is also assigned a room next to V's room
m = Const('m', members_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([m], Implies(And(m == W, Abs(assigned(m) - assigned(V)) == 1), Abs(assigned(R) - assigned(V)) == 1)))
m0 = Const('m0', members_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([m0], And(101 <= assigned(m0), assigned(m0) <= 107)))

# Question: Which one of the following CANNOT be assigned room 104?
def is_unsat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == unsat


# A) F
if is_unsat(assigned(F) == 104): print('(A)')
# B) G
if is_unsat(assigned(G) == 104): print('(B)')
# C) Q
if is_unsat(assigned(Q) == 104): print('(C)')
# D) S
if is_unsat(assigned(S) == 104): print('(D)')
# E) V
